Contact length 156cm: 114.0cm [13] 81. Tip length 156cm: 21.0cm [13] 82. Tail length 156cm: 21.0cm (same as tip — true twin) [13] 83. Sidecut type: Progressive sidecut — radius gets more aggressive closer to contact points [25] 84. Core material: Master Core — 1:1 Poplar to Paulownia ratio in alternating stringers [MERCHANT] [13] 85. Core wood species: Poplar and Paulownia (sustainably sourced) [13] 86. Core profiling: Softer between the feet for maneuverability, stiffer in tip and tail for stompability [13] 87. Fiberglass type: Biax (Biaxial) Fiberglass [MERCHANT] [13] 88. Fiberglass configuration: Dual-layer, dual-directional construction [13] 89. Laminate description: Delivers forgiving yet snappy board feel with mid-soft torsional flex and quick energy transfer [MERCHANT] 90. Carbon reinforcement: BComp Carbon Flax Stringer [MERCHANT] [13] 91. Carbon flax stringer detail: Carbon provides pop; flax absorbs chatter and reduces CO₂ emissions vs full carbon. Developed in collaboration with Swiss firm BComp [19] 92. Resin: Bio Resin — bio-based epoxy made with 27% plant-based carbon, reducing CO₂ emissions by 33% vs conventional epoxy [13] 93. Sidewall material: Recycled ABS with rounded finish [MERCHANT] [13] 94. Sidewall construction: Rounded finish engineered to reduce topsheet chipping and impact damage [13] 95. Edge material: Recycled German steel [MERCHANT] [13] 96. Base material: Sintered 8000 — Ultra High Molecular Weight Polyethylene and carbon [MERCHANT] [13] 97. Base type: Sintered (top-tier, fast, wax-absorbent, easy to repair, durable) [MERCHANT] 98. Topsheet: Premium Topsheet — durable and scratch-resistant [MERCHANT] [13] 99. Factory wax: WEND Natural Wax (plant-based, biodegradable, non-toxic) [MERCHANT] [13] 100. Factory tuning: De-tuned at tip and tail, edges angled at 90°/0°, ready to ride from factory [26] 101. Board break-in technology: Forever Flex — overbuilt then factory broken-in to mimic 20 days ridden [MERCHANT] [13] 102. Edge technology: Traction Tech — strategically placed contact points for improved edge grip on firm snow [MERCHANT] [13] 103. Edge technology detail (previous model): Traction Tech 3.0 features three bumps per edge (front binding, center, back binding); middle bump slightly bigger [26] 104. Nose design: Blunt nose — reduces swing weight for spinning, provides float benefits of longer nose without "snow plow" effect [13] 105. 3D base contouring philosophy: Inspired by surfboard design, reduces tip drag for effortless turns, better glide, enhanced float [MERCHANT] 106. Ride feel summary: "A fun, loose-ish playful ride that prefers moderate speeds to high speeds and favors maneuverability over stability" [27] 107. Pop: Easy to access pop, super effortless; not the highest total pop but most of what you get is gotten easily [28] 108. Catchiness: Very little catch risk — 3D Contour base with lifted edges plus soft torsional flex makes it nearly catch-free [27] 109. Turn initiation: Super easy to initiate turns; slashes effortlessly [27] 110. Carving performance: Carves well when not pushed too hard; edge can wash out at higher speeds under aggressive lean [27] 111. Edge hold on ice: Traction Tech edges are praised as a standout feature for icy conditions — "one of the top east coast park snowboards" [25] 112. High-speed stability: Not super stable at speed; gets wobbly at speeds faster than moderate [27] 113. Crud/chunder performance: Not super solid in rough snow; gets bucked around fairly easily but easy to make corrections [27] 114. Tree riding: Super fun in trees — very easy to make quick, sharp turns [27] 115. Powder performance: Decent in light powder; wouldn't be amazing in deeper powder [27] 116. Buttering/pressing: Extremely pressable — nose presses, tail presses, butters all come with ease [29] 117. Target speed range: Designed to shine at 15–25 mph according to Jeremy Jones himself [29] 118. Park performance: Outstanding for jumps, jibbing, rails — does both jumping and jibbing remarkably well [25] 119. Switch riding: True twin shape makes switch riding feel identical to regular [13] 120. New shape for 2027: Redesigned outline refined into a "more focused all-mountain freestyle twin" [30] 121. Improved tracking: "Cleaner tracking between turns and a more confident edge hold when you start pushing it" [30] 122. Broader versatility: "You can take it onto groomers, into side hits or through mixed conditions and it holds together in a way the previous version didn't quite manage" [30] 123. 3D Flip Tips (new for 2027): Help the board release cleanly so it doesn't feel grabby [30] 124. Full camber profile with 3D Flip Tips: Adds pop and versatility [4] 125. Board of the World rating (Tweaker): 92.55 out of 100 (4.62 out of 5); ranked 1st of 37 in all-mountain, 2nd of 28 in AM/freestyle, 3rd of 35 in park [25] 126. Board of the World top-6 AM freestyle twins list: Tweaker rated 4.29/5 [31] 127. Whitelines 100: Selected for Whitelines top 100 snowboard products (2022/23 and 2023/24) [3] 128. REI user rating (2024/25 Tweaker): 5.0 out of 5 stars (1 review) [16] 129. Jones.com user rating: 4.9 out of 5 (52 reviews) [13] 130. The Inertia verdict: "A true quiver-killer for riders who lean all-mountain freestyle"; described as "severely underrated" [32] 131. Snowboarder Magazine review: Praised pop, pressability, edge hold; recommended for park riders, side-hit hunters, daily drivers at smaller areas [29] 132. The Good Ride review: Described as "very easy twin to ride with a short learning curve"; noted spoon tech can be "washy and a little edgeless in harder snow" [33] 133. Edge hold praised: "I am always impressed by the level of edge hold in the board and how well it carves, given that its main focus is for park riding" [25] 134. Catch-free feel: Board feels "grippy when it needs to be as well as catch-free and skate-like while it's flat on its base" [25] 135. Versatility: "Outstanding board both in and out of the park" — excels at both jumping and jibbing, rare for a park board [25] 136. Approachable: "Great for trying new things with confidence" due to low-consequence ride feel [27] 137. Build quality / eco credentials: Praised for premium construction at an approachable price with strong sustainability story [32] 138. Euro carving capability: Reviewer achieved Euro carves after adjustment period despite soft flex [29] 139. Limited stability at speed: Board gets "wobbly" at higher speeds — expected for soft flex [27] 140. Rough snow performance: Gets bucked around in crud/chunder; not super solid [27] 141. Edge washout: Edge can wash out at higher speeds when leaning hard, especially on hard snow [27] 142. Big air limitations: Landing from bigger air isn't as solid; lots of flex in tip/tail can be limiting for large jumps [28] 143. Not for beginners: Despite friendly flex, the loose feel may be harder to control for those starting out [27] 144. Spoon base washiness: "That spoon tech can be washy and a little edgeless in harder snow" [33] 145. Comparable board: Burton Process — "another all-mountain board that rides similarly with comparable versatility" [32] 146. Comparable board: CAPiTA Defenders of Awesome (DOA) — "another freestyle legend with all-mountain chops" [34] 147. Comparable board: Nitro T1 — "a classic park twin with a loyal following" [34] 148. Comparable board: Bataleon Evil Twin — "playful 3BT shaping for creative freestyle riders" [34] 149. Jones Tweaker Pro (variant): Stiffer (7/10 flex vs 4/10), Koroyd-dampened core, faster Sintered base; $629.95 USD; for more aggressive riders [14][35] 150. Jones Mountain Twin: Directional twin with setback stance; more all-mountain focused vs Tweaker's freestyle focus [36] 151. Jones Rally Cat: Directional twin, similarly soft flex, suited to beginner-to-intermediate riders [32] 152. Jones Snowboards (direct): Official manufacturer store, $529.95 USD (2026), free shipping over $100, 30-day returns, extended warranty [13] 153. Melbourne Snowboard Centre (AU): Authorized dealer, AUD $949.99, local independent store, 30-day credit/exchange policy [2] 154. Balmoral Boards (AU): Authorized dealer, pre-order available, $10 flat-rate AU shipping, lay-by available [17] 155. Ballistyx (AU): Melbourne store since 1991, preorder includes bonus T-shirt [18] 156. NZ Shred (NZ): NZ retailer, authorized dealer [19] 157. BaseNZ (NZ): NZ retailer [20] 158. Milo Sport (US, SLC): Authorized Jones dealer, pickup available [21] 159. evo (US): Major retailer, free shipping, lowest price guarantee (beat by 5%), 1-year return policy [22] 160. REI (US): Carried prior year models; 2024/25 now discontinued [16] 161. Backcountry (US): Carried discounted prior models at ~$424–$504 [15] 162. Jones Snowboards founding year: 2010 [6] 163. Jones Tweaker original introduction: 2022/23 season (first dedicated park/freestyle board in Jones lineup) [3][25] 164. Tweaker 2.0 designation: 2027 is the first year of the "2.0" redesign [4] 165. Design philosophy: "Change your board, change your mountain" — each board built for a distinct experience-driven feel [4] 166. Lifecycle analysis: Jones is one of the only snowsports manufacturers to conduct a full lifecycle analysis of its boards [37] 167. Recycled ABS sidewalls: Used since 2014; 847 miles of recycled sidewalls used [26]
